scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

pre_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the inter-router WAN link between router0 and router1, specifically router1’s eth2 (10.10.0.2) interface. Mechanism: The IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) VLANs hang off router0 and depend on the r0–r1 link to reach all other networks. With router1 eth2 down, router0 cannot reach the rest of the campus, so hosts in IT/CS get “Destination Host Unreachable” generated by their default gateway (192.168.1.1/192.168.2.1). Meanwhile, networks behind router1 and router2 (Office 192.168.3.0/24, Principle 192.168.4.0/24, Servers 1.0.0.0/8, Internet Lab 128.168.0.0/16) still reach each other via the healthy r1–r2 link (20.20.0.0/8), matching observed behavior.

Localization: On router1, eth2 shows state DOWN with IP 10.10.0.2; on router0, eth2 is UP at 10.10.0.1. A ping from router0 to 10.10.0.2 fails 100% (link broken). Pings from it_hod/cs_hod to external networks return “From 192.168.1.1/192.168.2.1 Destination Host Unreachable.” Conversely, TPO and Office PCs can reach Internet Lab and Principle (confirmed successful pings).

Root cause: router1’s eth2 (wan_r0_r1 side) is down, severing connectivity between router0 and the rest of the network.

Corrective fix: Bring router1 eth2 back up (e.g., ip link set dev eth2 up) and verify L2 on wan_r0_r1. Then confirm 10.10.0.1↔10.10.0.2 reachability and that IT/CS routes propagate. Optionally restart FRR to refresh RIP adjacencies if routes have become stale.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names the inter-router WAN link between router0 and router1 and identifies router1's eth2 (10.10.0.2) on the 10.10.0.0/8 link as affected.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states that only the IT/CS subnets (192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24) lose reachability while networks behind router1/router2 (Office/Principle/Servers/Internet Lab) remain reachable, matching the required symptom distinction.
Correctly recommends bringing router1 eth2 up (ip link set dev eth2 up) and verifying L2/reachability and routes, matching the expected fix.

The investigation provides direct evidence (failed ping from router0 to 10.10.0.2, gateway-generated “Destination Host Unreachable” on IT/CS, and successful pings among networks behind router1/router2) that the r0–r1 WAN is the point of failure, but the agent asserts router1’s eth2 is DOWN without a recorded interface-state check on router1 and does not reconcile the observed FRR service inactivity.
